verses.1:1: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect and the full knowledge of the truth that conforms to godliness,
verses.1:2: in the hope of eternal life, which God, who does not lie, promised before eternal ages,
verses.1:3: and in His own proper times manifested His word through the proclamation with which I was entrusted, according to the command of God our Savior,
verses.1:4: To Titus, a true child in our common faith: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
verses.1:5: For this reason I left you behind in Crete, that you might put in order the things that remain lacking, and appoint elders in every city just as I directed you:
verses.1:6: if anyone is beyond reproach, the husband of one wife, having faithful children, not under a charge of dissipation nor rebellious.
verses.1:7: For an overseer must be beyond reproach, as a steward of God—not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not given to wine, not a brawler, not eager for shameful gain;
verses.1:8: but hospitable, a lover of what is good, sober-minded, upright, devout, self-controlled,
verses.1:9: holding steadfastly to the trustworthy word according to the teaching, so that he may be able both to exhort in sound doctrine and to refute those who contradict it.
verses.1:10: For there are many unruly men, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision,
verses.1:11: whose mouths must be silenced, who overturn whole households, teaching things they ought not to teach for the sake of shameful gain.
verses.1:12: One from among them, a prophet of their own, said, "Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons."
verses.1:13: This testimony is true. For this cause reprove them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,
verses.1:14: not giving heed to Jewish myths and commandments of men who turn away from the truth.
verses.1:15: All things are pure to those who are pure; yet to the defiled and unbelieving nothing is pure, but both their mind and their conscience have been defiled.
verses.1:16: They profess to know God, yet by their works they deny Him, being detestable, disobedient, and disqualified for every good work.
verses.2:1: But as for you, speak the things that befit sound doctrine:
verses.2:2: that older men be temperate, dignified, sober-minded, sound in faith, in love, and in steadfastness.
verses.2:3: Older women likewise are to be reverent in demeanor, not slanderers nor enslaved to much wine, teachers of what is good,
verses.2:4: so that they may instruct the younger women to love their husbands and to love their children,
verses.2:5: to be sober-minded, pure, workers at home, kind, and subject to their own husbands, so that the word of God may not be reviled.
verses.2:6: Likewise, exhort the younger men to be sober-minded;
verses.2:7: in all things presenting yourself as a pattern of good works; in your teaching showing integrity, dignity,
verses.2:8: and sound speech beyond condemnation, so that the opponent may be put to shame, having nothing evil to say about us.
verses.2:9: Bondservants are to be subject to their own masters in everything, to be well-pleasing, not contradicting,
verses.2:10: not pilfering, but displaying all good fidelity, so that in every way they may adorn the doctrine of God our Savior.
verses.2:11: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all mankind,
verses.2:12: instructing us that, renouncing ungodliness and worldly desires, we should live soberly, uprightly, and godly in this present age,
verses.2:13: awaiting the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,
verses.2:14: who gave Himself for us, that He might redeem us from all lawlessness and purify for Himself a people peculiarly His own, zealous for good works.
verses.2:15: Speak these things, exhort, and reprove with full authority; let no one disregard you.
verses.3:1: Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,
verses.3:2: to malign no one, to be peaceable and forbearing, displaying all meekness toward all mankind.
verses.3:3: For we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, and led astray, enslaved to various desires and pleasures, spending our days in malice and envy, detestable and hating one another.
verses.3:4: But when the kindness and love for mankind of God our Savior appeared,
verses.3:5: not by works done in righteousness that we ourselves performed, but according to His mercy He saved us, through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit,
verses.3:6: whom He poured out bountifully upon us through Jesus Christ our Savior,
verses.3:7: so that, having been justified by His grace, we may become heirs in keeping with the hope of eternal life.
verses.3:8: This saying is trustworthy, and concerning these things I desire you to speak with firm conviction, so that those who have believed in God may be careful to devote themselves to good works. These things are excellent and profitable for mankind.
verses.3:9: But shun foolish controversies, genealogies, dissensions, and quarrels about the law, for they are unprofitable and futile.
verses.3:10: After a first and second warning, reject a factious person,
verses.3:11: knowing that such a one has been perverted and goes on sinning, standing self-condemned.
verses.3:12: When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to winter there.
verses.3:13: Diligently help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey, so that they may lack nothing.
verses.3:14: And let our own people also learn to devote themselves to good works to meet urgent needs, so that they may not be unfruitful.
verses.3:15: All who are with me send you greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with all of you.

notes.1:4: The critical Greek text reads 'Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior,' omitting 'mercy' and 'the Lord' found in later Byzantine manuscripts.
notes.1:6: The Greek adjective translated 'faithful' (pista) can mean either 'believing' (Christian) or 'trustworthy/faithful' in conduct.
notes.1:12: Paul quotes a hexameter line attributed to the sixth-century BC Cretan poet and seer Epimenides of Knossos.
notes.2:5: The earliest manuscripts read oikourgous ('workers at home' or 'busy at home'), whereas some later manuscripts read oikourous ('keepers at home').
notes.2:11: Without the definite article before soterios, the phrase reads 'has appeared, bringing salvation to all mankind,' though 'to all mankind' may modify either 'bringing salvation' or 'has appeared.'
notes.2:13: A single Greek definite article governs both 'great God' and 'Savior' (tou megalou theou kai soteros hemon), directly identifying Jesus Christ as both God and Savior.
notes.3:5: The phrase 'washing of regeneration' (loutron palingenesias) may also be rendered 'washing of rebirth,' and the genitive 'of the Holy Spirit' may qualify 'renewal' or both 'washing' and 'renewal.'
notes.3:10: The Greek hairetikon anthropon denotes a 'factious' or 'divisive' person who stirs up schisms within the church rather than the later technical sense of a doctrinal heretic alone.
notes.3:15: The earliest Greek manuscripts conclude the letter with 'Grace be with all of you,' without a final 'Amen.'
